input: Scheduled routine: continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products in production; merge when done.
task: Deepen (flagship 9): league-schedule-generator -- weekend tournament scheduler (multi-division pools and brackets on shared fields)

doc_friction.issue: --history TEXT removed the named result from flagships.yaml `next:` but wrote nothing to the venture's HISTORY.md (checked with git diff); I appended the line by hand. Its --make-room also parked a landed clause ('two courses 2026-11-20') into NEXT.md's open items.

league-schedule-generator's `next:` is almost all landed-history and long-tail combinatorics (49 teams on 8x9 bowling etc.); the row pointed at no user-facing gap, so finding a worthwhile item meant reading README headings and guessing which workflow users lack.

deviations.why: The row's listed open items are combinatorial edge cases (bowling 47/49 on 8x9, carry-over bounds) or need real inputs; marginal value to users is low after 110 commits in 7 days.
deviations.did: Built a new workflow inside the flagship instead: a multi-division weekend tournament scheduler (pools, crossover brackets, field sizes, rest, daily cap, coaches), a page, an eval and a post.
deviations.result: Landed with tests and a 400-weekend measurement; flagship next: rewritten to name it.

goal: Give tournament directors a free scheduler for multi-division weekends, a workflow paid tournament platforms sell.
notes: Checks run here: node --test tournament.test.mjs (9 pass), node --test page.test.mjs (61 pass), python3 platform/ci/check_posts.py ok, portfolio/router/validate.py ok, page loaded in Chromium at 390 px (36 games, no console errors, scrollWidth 390). eval/tournament-search.mjs seeds 1 and 2 (output in eval/tournament-search.txt): on 160 no-warning weekends all games placed 92.9%/96.1% at 120 tries vs 83.3%/88.2% one pass; 194 warned weekends never fully placed; 0 invalid. Full venture suite and venture-preflight: see PR body.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a senior engineer building a multi-division tournament scheduler with constraint checks, eval, page and docs: about three days

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
